chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Hakam, from Abu Abdillah or Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man divorces his wife, and when three months pass, she claims to be pregnant.' He said, 'Wait with her for nine months.' I said, 'And if she claims pregnancy after that?' He said, 'Far be it, far be it! The cessation of menstruation is of two types: either clear pregnancy, or irregularity from menstruation. But she should observe precautionary waiting for three months afterwards.'
And he also said regarding the woman who used to menstruate, then her menstruation ceases for a year: 'How is she divorced?' He said, 'She is divorced by witnesses.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a divorced woman with irregular menstruation who claims pregnancy?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the fiqh of 'iddah for a divorced woman with irregular menstruation (muṭallaqa dhāt al-ʿiddeh al-mutaghayyirah), distinguishing between clear pregnancy and menstrual irregularity. It establishes that while a claim of pregnancy after three months warrants a nine-month wait, the cessation of menses is generally attributed to either pregnancy or irregularity, requiring a three-month precautionary period before finalizing the divorce. Furthermore, it addresses the scenario where menstruation ceases for a year, ruling that the divorce is finalized through the testimony of witnesses, reflecting the Shia juristic approach to resolving uncertainty in waiting periods.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sia, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Hakeem, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, or Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man divorces his wife. So when three months pass by, she claims to be pregnant’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should wait with her for nine months’. I said, ‘So if she claim after to be pregnant?’ He<sup>asws</sup> Far be it! Far be it! But rather, the lifting of the menstruation is of two types – Either a pregnancy is manifested, or there is a spoiling from the menstruations. But, she should be precautionary by three months afterwards’.

And he (the narrator) said as well: ‘Regarding the woman who menstruates, then her menstruation is lifted for a year, how would she be divorced?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would be divorced by the witnesses?’
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Hakim who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, or abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his wife and after three months she claims to be pregnant. He (the Imam) said, ‘There is a waiting for her for nine months.’ I then said, ‘She has claimed to be pregnant after that. He (the Imam) said, ‘This is far from reality. Hayd (menses) stops for two reasons, because of a clear pregnancy or disorder in Hayd. However, she can remain cautious for three months thereafter.’ “
He (the narrator) also asked about a woman who experienced Hayd and then it stopped after one year and about how she is divorced. He (the Imam) said, ‘She is divorced in the presence of witnesses.’”

(The following paragraph does not seem to be part of Hadith ) Certain ones have said that if he wants to divorce her, she does not experience Hayd (menses) and he has gone to bed with her; he can place her in quarantine. He must hold back from her for three months from the time a divorced woman becomes stranger to her husband, a woman whose Hayd (menses) is straight if pregnancy becomes clear, otherwise, he can divorce her once in the presence of two witnesses. If he leaves her for three months she becomes stranger by one divorce. If he wants to divorce her three times, he can leave her for one month, then go back to her, then divorce her for the second time, then hold back from her three months to place her in quarantine; if pregnancy becomes clear thereafter he only has to divorce her once.”
